# BioNexus end-to-end scientific case studies

This directory is the publication gate for the six demonstration workflows requested in the scientific roadmap. The registry deliberately distinguishes a **protocol-ready** case study from an **executed/validated** case study. A workflow that merely runs is not promoted to scientific evidence.

## Promotion rule

A case study may move from `protocol-ready` to `executed` only after its exact input files and SHA-256 checksums, database/reference releases, BioNexus experiment ID, git commit, container/environment fingerprint, random seed where relevant, parameter snapshot, raw outputs, output checksums, complete provenance graph, statistical report and BBS-2 benchmark run are archived. It may move to `validated` only when its predeclared ground-truth comparator and acceptance criteria pass. Failed cases remain in the archive.

The six registered workflows are rare-disease variant interpretation, protein-family functional annotation, drug repurposing against a validated target, primer design with downstream validation, comparative microbial genomics, and RNA-seq differential expression with pathway interpretation. Their machine-readable definitions live in `case_studies.json`.

## Required result package

Each executed case-study directory should contain `input-manifest.json`, `experiment-archive.json`, `provenance.json`, `benchmark-result.json`, `statistics.json`, `figures/`, `supplementary/`, `methods.md`, `results.md`, `limitations.md`, and `SHA256SUMS`. The experiment archive generated by BioNexus is the source of truth for code/tool/database/environment metadata.

## Scientific boundaries

Clinical or therapeutic language is prohibited unless it is directly supported by the predefined external evidence set and the demonstration is explicitly labelled research-only. A rare-disease workflow cannot be called a diagnostic validation study merely because variant calls agree with a small fixture. A docking or MD workflow cannot be presented as evidence that a compound is effective. Synthetic fixtures are valid for deterministic regression but must never be described as biological validation.
